slides.title: Language Focus — Imagery, Repetition & Contractions
slides.content:
Kanye writes his testimony using three tools you can hear all over "God Is". Spotting them will help you understand hip-hop, gospel and spoken English in general.
• Metaphor — physical images stand for spiritual experiences (light = hope, race = life, fountain = renewal).
• Anaphora — starting several lines with the same words ("I know…", "This my…") to build emotional weight.
• Colloquial contractions — 'em (them), 'bout (about) and ain't (isn't / aren't) are common in songs and casual speech, not in formal writing.
Read each example and notice what the writer really means, not just the literal words.

words.example: Metaphor: "light" = hope / God; "darkness" = fear or struggle. Not literal light.

words.word: He's the strength in this race that I run
words.example: Metaphor: life is compared to a long race — endurance, effort, a finish line.

words.word: I know God is the force that picked me up / I know Christ is the fountain that filled my cup
words.example: Anaphora: both lines start with "I know" for testimony emphasis. Also two metaphors: force lifting + fountain filling.

words.word: This my kids, this the crib, this my wife, this my life
words.example: Anaphora: "This my…" repeats four times. In casual/hip-hop English the verb "is" is often dropped ("this [is] my life").

words.word: All my idols, let 'em go / All the demons, let 'em know
words.example: 'em = them (colloquial contraction). Common in spoken English and songs — never in academic writing.
ain't = isn't / aren't; 'bout = about. Two contractions in five words — very informal, very typical of hip-hop.

slides.title: Free Practice — Production
slides.prompt: Now it's your turn. Answer in your own words — take your time and be honest.
slides.content:
Kanye repeats 'I know' many times. Is there something in your life you feel absolutely certain about? What is it, and why?
The song says 'You won't ever be the same when you call on Jesus' name'. Have you ever had an experience that changed you completely — spiritual, personal or something else?
Kanye lists what matters to him: "This my kids, this the crib, this my wife, this my life". If you had to write a similar line about YOUR life, what four things would you include?
In one sentence, what do you think Kanye is really saying in this song?

slides.prompt: How did the song "God Is" make you feel? Did it match your predictions?
slides.title: Wrap Up
slides.content:
→ What was the most interesting expression you learned?
→ Would you recommend this song to a friend? Why?
→ How does the song connect to your own life?
